students.overall_feedback: The student demonstrates a strong grasp of multi-step financial arithmetic, executed with high accuracy in Item 1 Part (a). Similarly, the division of net income to determine individual member profit shares was well executed and clearly set out. However, the student's primary weakness lies in analytical interpretation and coordinate geometry derivations. In Item 1 Part (b), the candidate incorrectly compared gross revenue from a flat-rate strategy against the net profit of phased sales, leading to a flawed conclusion that flat-rate pricing was superior. Furthermore, in Item 2 Part (a), the candidate failed to apply the standard distance formula to determine the side lengths of the triangle, arbitrarily assuming side dimensions of nine, nine, and eight meters instead of calculating exact values from the given coordinates. Secondary observations include incomplete final steps, such as omitting the final summation for total material cost in Item 2 despite correctly calculating the individual unit costs for fencing rolls and fertilizer bags.
